## Mission

The EMPRESS Research Network is a multicenter, internationally collaborative clinical research network initiated by the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Sichuan Academy of Medical Sciences and Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital, dedicated to **improving the critical care of septic shock**. The network's core mission is to conduct high-quality multicenter clinical trials, while also providing methodological support, data governance, and investigator training. The first study of the network is the EMPRESS trial &mdash; a multicenter randomized controlled trial evaluating whether early administration of methylene blue reduces mortality in patients with high-dose vasopressor-dependent septic shock.

## Organization

- **Lead institution**: Department of Critical Care Medicine, Sichuan Academy of Medical Sciences and Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China); serves as sponsor and coordinating center
- **Study centers**: more than 50 tertiary hospital centers across China (emergency, respiratory, medical, surgical, and other ICUs)
- **International collaboration**: the Steering Committee includes international members from the United Kingdom, France, Chile, Mexico, and Ireland (see [Governance](governance.html))
- **Governance bodies**: Steering Committee, Coordinating Committee, Data Safety Monitoring Board (see [Governance](governance.html))

## Research Areas

1. Mechanisms and targeted therapy of vasoplegia in septic and distributive shock
2. Clinical evaluation of catecholamine-sparing strategies (methylene blue, vasopressin, etc.)
3. Methodology and data governance for multicenter clinical trials

## Data and Quality

The network follows international standards of clinical trials (ICH-GCP) and applicable regulations. Key documents, including the study protocol, statistical analysis plan, and interim reports, are reviewed by the Steering Committee and published in the [Documents](documents.html) section. Study registration and ethics information are verifiable in public registries.
